'''''Grevillea rosmarinifolia''''', commonly known as '''rosemary grevillea''',<ref name="RBGS">{{cite web |last1=Makinson |first1=Robert O. |title=''Grevillea rosmarinifolia'' |url=https://plantnet.rbgsyd.nsw.gov.au/cgi-bin/NSWfl.pl?page=nswfl&lvl=sp&name=Grevillea~rosmarinifolia |publisher=Royal Botanic Garden Sydney |access-date=1 January 2023}}</ref> is a species of flowering plant in the family [[Proteaceae]] and is [[endemic]] to south-eastern continental Australia and naturalised in other parts of the country. It is usually an erect, compact to open shrub with linear, narrowly elliptic or narrowly oblong leaves with the edges rolled under, and loose clusters of pink to red flowers.

==Description==
''Grevillea rosmarinifolia'' is usually an erect, compact to open, sometimes low shrub that typically grows to a height of {{cvt|0.3–2|m}}. Its leaves are linear to narrowly elliptic or narrowly oblong, {{cvt|8–38|mm}} long and {{cvt|0.7–3|mm}} wide with the edges rolled under, usually concealing the lower surface. The flowers are arranged on the ends of the branches, usually in groups of 4 to 12 on a [[wikt:glabrous|glabrous]] [[rachis]] {{cvt|2–8|mm}} long. The flowers are pink to red, the [[Gynoecium#Pistils|pistil]] {{cvt|15–22.5|mm}} long. Flowering occurs from August to December, and the fruit is a hairy, oblong [[Follicle (fruit)|follicle]] {{cvt|8–11|mm}} long.<ref name="foa">{{cite web |title=''Grevillea rosmarinifolia'' |url=https://profiles.ala.org.au/opus/foa/profile/Grevillea%20rosmarinifolia |publisher=Australian Biological Resources Study, Department of Agriculture, Water and the Environment: Canberra |access-date=1 January 2023}}</ref><ref name="Wrigley">{{cite book |last1=Wrigley |first1=John W. |last2=Fagg |first2=Murray A. |title=Banksias, waratahs & grevilleas : and all other plants in the Australian Proteaceae family |date=1991 |publisher=Angus & Robertson |location=North Ryde, NSW, Australia |isbn=0207172773 |pages=322–323}}</ref><ref name="anpsa">{{cite web |title=''Grevillea rosmarinifolia'' |url=https://anpsa.org.au/plant_profiles/grevillea-rosmarinifolia/ |publisher=Australian Native Plants Society (Australia) |access-date=1 January 2023}}</ref><ref name="RBGV">{{cite web |last1=Makinson |first1=Robert O. |last2=Stajsic |first2=Val |title=''Grevillea rosmarinifolia'' |url=https://vicflora.rbg.vic.gov.au/flora/taxon/4936d954-8945-41d9-8e59-315bd11a9fe5 |publisher=Royal Botanic Gardens Victoria |access-date=2 January 2023}}</ref>

==Taxonomy==
''Grevillea rosmarinifolia'' was first formally described in 1825 by [[Allan Cunningham (botanist)|Allan Cunningham]], in [[Barron Field (author)|Barron Field's]] book, ''Geographical Memoirs on New South Wales'', from specimens collected on the banks of the [[Coxs River]].<ref name=APNI>{{cite web|title=''Grevillea rosmarinifolia''|url= https://id.biodiversity.org.au/instance/apni/457313 |publisher=APNI|access-date=1 January 2023}}</ref><ref name="Field">{{cite book |editor-last=Field |editor-first=Barron |last1=Cunningham |first1=Allan |title=Geographical Memoirs on New South Wales |date=1825 |publisher=John Murray |location=London |page=350 |url=http://gutenberg.net.au/ebooks13/1304421h.html |access-date=1 January 2023 | via=Project Gutenberg Australia}}</ref> The [[Binomial nomenclature|specific epithet]] (''rosmarinifolia'') means "[[rosemary]]-leaved".<ref name="Sharr">{{cite book |last1=Sharr |first1=Francis Aubi |last2=George |first2=Alex |title=Western Australian Plant Names and Their Meanings |date=2019 |publisher=Four Gables Press |location=Kardinya, WA |isbn=9780958034180 |page=297 |edition=3rd}}</ref>

==Distribution and habitat==
Rosemary grevillea is native to [[New South Wales]] and [[Victoria (Australia)|Victoria]], but is naturalised in [[South Australia]] and the [[Australian Capital Territory]].<ref name="APC" /> Subspecies ''glabella'' grows in mallee or shrubland in sandy soils in the [[Rankins Springs]] to [[Griffith, New South Wales|Griffith]] area of southern New South Wales and in the [[Little Desert]] area of western Victoria.<ref name="RBGS1" /><ref name="foa1" /><ref name="RBGV1" /> Subspecies ''rosmarinifolia'' grows in open forest or woodland in [[montane]] areas of south-eastern New South Wales and in isolated areas of inland Victoria, between [[Gippsland]], [[Melbourne]], [[Skipton]] and the [[Brisbane Ranges]].<ref name="RBGS2" /><ref name="foa2" /><ref name="RBGV2" />

==Use in horticulture==
This grevillea is common in cultivation and all forms are readily grown from cuttings. The [[Type (biology)|type]] form from the Coxs River is thought to be extinct in the field, but was rediscovered by [[Donald McGillivray (botanist)|Donald McGillivray]] growing outside the [[Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh]] in 1969. 
''Grevillea rosmarinifolia'' prefers full sun. It is drought tolerant and hardy down to {{convert|-10 |C|F|abbr=on}}. In the [[UK]] it has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref name = RHSPF>{{cite web |url= https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/8115/i-Grevillea-rosmarinifolia-i/Details |title = RHS Plantfinder - ''Grevillea rosmarinifolia'' | access-date=16 February 2018}}</ref>
